newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INTERVIEW-Progressive sees lift in profit.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Progressive sees lift in profit.

text.p: Progressive Enterprises Ltd Chief Executive Graeme Kelly said on Friday the company expected to report a substantial lift in earnings over the first half, in the 1996/7 financial year and in 1997/8.

He also told Reuters in an interview that the supermarket chain had remedied its breach of interest rate covenants with its banks and had reduced debt by about NZ$70-80 million from a peak of NZ$210 million a year ago.
The improved and stable trading position had allowed the company to pullback on its asset divestment programme.

Analysts have forecast a first half result of around $6.0-7.5 million and Kelly said the company expected to do a little better than that. "We are not uncomfortable with having those sorts of forecasts out in the market place," he said.
He expected a similar performance in the second half, giving a July 31, 1997 year result that analysts have put at NZ$15-20 million.

"Looking out to 1998, if you take a profit of that order, with the understanding that we are still carrying Georgie Pie at run rate loss of about NZ$8-10 million a year and take it out of next year's result...then you've got potential for a 50 percent increase again without doing anything else.

"If you work those numbers through, NZ$5.0 million last year, analysts forecasts of NZ$15-20 million this year and $25-30 million in 1997/8, you are getting the order of magnitude of improvement that we are working to achieve and believe is realistic to achieve."

Progressive, struggling under the weight of its loss-making Georgie Pie operation, plus operational problems, made a NZ$2.2 million net profit in the first half to January last year. Progressive came under new management in February and many, like Kelly, had previous experience with the company.
Costs had been controlled and the company was at a point where many of the variables assumed by some analysts had changed.

Analysts are now moving to quite positive views of the company, he said. One Australian analyst had concluded that NZ$1.40 a share was fair value while another had estimated fair value at between NZ$1.50-60. Progressive traded today at $1.42.
Kelly said the company was now seeing flow-on effects of the remedial programme undertaken by the company.
"So the prospects looking out into 1998, with that Georgie Pie problem fixed, are quite good," he said.
Kelly said said he was comfortable, at this stage of the "restoration and recovery" cycle, with flat sales over the quarter to January 26.

"Our focus is not on growing the market share that we have, our focus is on maybe more profit than what we've got. We need to perform much more profitably. And until we are, I think we should continue to focus on profit restoration."
Progressive is 57 percent owned by Foodland Associated.
